help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The start of the run was delayed by the fans' shouting.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The bus driver called the police immediately.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Nouns made from the bare verb stem are masculine: der Sprung, der Lauf, der Beginn.
help.tips[0].en.text: -er = the person: Lehrer, Fahrer, Leser, Spieler. Stem = the event: der Lauf, der Beginn, der Schlaf, der Fall, der Ruf, der Sprung. Ge-…-e = the constant activity, often annoying: das Gerede, das Geschrei, das Gelaufe, das Getue.
help.tips[0].en.title: Types 1–3: -er (der), stem (der), Ge-…-e (das)
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: While reading the decision I had a question and asked for help.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The search for a flat has already lasted half a year.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The capitalised infinitive names the activity itself; der Lauf is one run and das Gelaufe is annoying running about.
help.tips[1].en.text: Infinitive = the activity, always possible: das Lesen, das Schwimmen, das Warten. -e = the act or thing: die Hilfe, die Frage, die Bitte, die Suche, die Reise. -ung = process or result, the most common: die Prüfung, die Entscheidung, die Lösung, die Übung, die Bedeutung.
help.tips[1].en.title: Types 4–6: Infinitiv (das), -e (die), -ung (die)
help.tips[1].en.trap: the same verb can give several nouns with different meanings: laufen → der Lauf (a run), das Laufen (running), das Gelaufe (all that running about). The suffix chooses the meaning.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Passengers are asked to heed what was said – to avoid waiting times.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Many students suffer from exam nerves.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: After -ung a compound takes the Fugen-s: Wohnung + s + Suche.
help.tips[2].en.text: After -ung / -heit / -keit / -schaft / -ion / -tät the compound takes -s-: Prüfungsangst, Entscheidungsfreiheit, Freundschaftsdienst, Universitätsstadt. Participles as nouns: der Angestellte, die Reisenden, das Gesagte, das Erreichte.
help.tips[2].en.title: Fugen-s and participle nouns
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: runner – run – running about – running – (tiresome) running around
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: one noun of each gender pair
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: A capitalised infinitive is always neuter: das Warten.
help.tips[3].en.text: -er der · stem der · Ge-e das · Infinitiv das · -e die · -ung die. Two masculine, two neuter, two feminine — a symmetric system.
help.tips[3].en.title: Gender by type
help.context.en: Before the exam, studying was my whole life: reading in the morning, the search for answers at noon, the help of my flatmates in the evening. The others' talk about the start of the holidays didn't bother me. On the day of the decision I was first at the door – exam nerves had turned me into a runner.
help.hookEn: Turn any verb into a noun six ways and know its gender from how it was built: der Lauf, das Laufen, die Lösung.
help.introEn: Turning verbs into nouns is the engine of written German — Nominalstil — and there are six ways to do it, each with its own gender. (1) -er for the doer: lehren → der Lehrer, fahren → der Fahrer (masculine; -in for women). (2) The bare verb stem, often with a vowel change: laufen → der Lauf, beginnen → der Beginn, schlafen → der Schlaf, fallen → der Fall (masculine). (3) Ge- + stem + -e for repeated or annoying activity: reden → das Gerede, schreien → das Geschrei, laufen → das Gelaufe (neuter, usually pejorative). (4) The capitalised infinitive for the activity itself: lesen → das Lesen, schwimmen → das Schwimmen (neuter, always available). (5) Stem + -e: helfen → die Hilfe, fragen → die Frage, bitten → die Bitte, suchen → die Suche (feminine). (6) -ung for the process or result: prüfen → die Prüfung, entscheiden → die Entscheidung, üben → die Übung (feminine, the most productive). Compounds join with a Fugen-s after -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion: Prüfungsangst, Entscheidungshilfe. Participles nominalise too: der Angestellte, die Reisenden, das Gesagte. Reading, these let you unpack a dense phrase; writing, they let you compress a clause — and later in the course the reverse operation (Verbalisierung) becomes a full skill.
help.rememberEn[0]: -er / stem = der; Ge-e / Infinitiv = das; -e / -ung = die.
sentences[1].whyEn: beginnen → der Beginn — the verb stem as a noun, masculine.
sentences[2].whyEn: Ge- + -e disparages: das Gerede — annoying endless talk.
sentences[3].whyEn: A nominalised infinitive, always das: beim Schwimmen.
sentences[7].whyEn: entscheiden + -ung: die Entscheidung — and you 'meet' it.
sentences[8].whyEn: The single event: der Lauf — not das Laufen (the activity).
sentences[11].whyEn: A compound with linking s: die Prüfungsangst.
sentences[12].whyEn: An adjective as a noun, plural after die: die Angestellten.
sentences[13].whyEn: suchen → die Suche — with nach, like the verb.
sentences[14].whyEn: schlafen → der Schlaf — the stem as a masculine noun.
sentences[15].whyEn: Ge- + -e(ll): das Gebell — the annoying nonstop barking.
sentences[16].whyEn: ankommen → die Ankunft — an irregular nominalisation.
